sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Mass Mobilization**: The CDM witnessed unprecedented participation from women, students, youth, and rural peasantry, marking a shift from the urban-centric Non-Cooperation Movement.
• **Economic Drivers**: The Great Depression (1929) acted as a catalyst, pushing the agrarian class into the movement due to falling crop prices and rigid land revenue demands.
• **Strategic Settlement**: The 'Possibility of Settlement' was defined by the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931), which served as a tactical pause rather than a surrender, testing the British willingness to recognize the INC as the sole representative of India.
• **Key Metric**: The movement's success was measured by the 'depth' of participation (rural penetration) rather than just the 'breadth' (urban protests).

items.definition: A political settlement where the INC agreed to suspend the CDM and participate in the Second Round Table Conference in exchange for the release of political prisoners and the right to make salt.
The mechanism of 'Struggle-Truce-Struggle' (S-T-S) strategy, where the movement is paused to allow for negotiations, preventing the exhaustion of the masses.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Salt Satyagraha**: A symbolic yet potent mechanism to unite diverse castes and classes under a single economic grievance.
• **No-Tax/No-Rent Campaigns**: Direct challenge to the colonial state's fiscal legitimacy.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Communal divide (Muslim participation was lower compared to NCM), and the lack of a unified agrarian program.
• **Solutions**: Integration of socio-economic reforms (Constructive Programme) to sustain long-term engagement.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'W-P-B-S' (Women, Peasantry, Business, Students).
• **Decoded Meaning**: These were the four pillars of the CDM. Remember: Women picketed, Peasants protested, Businessmen petitioned, Students participated.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often claims the Muslim participation was as high as in the Non-Cooperation Movement. This is false; Muslim participation was significantly lower due to the influence of the Muslim League and the Khilafat issue being absent.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Struggle-Truce-Struggle' (Bipan Chandra's framework) to explain why the INC entered into the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

keyTakeaways: The CDM was the first movement where the INC successfully mobilized the rural masses on a national scale.
The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was a tactical settlement that validated the INC's status as a legitimate political entity.
Participation was uneven across regions and communities, with significant gaps in Muslim-majority areas.
